patterns.platform: Squarespace search block (instant/predictive results)
patterns.name: Instant search results render with no announcement or result count
patterns.description: Results appear on each keystroke beneath the search box, but the results container is not a live region and the result count is never announced, so screen-reader users don't know results appeared, how many, or that the list changed. The Quick Preview is also keyboard-inaccessible and the spinner is silent.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static analysis finds a labeled search input and valid result links. The absence of an announcement is a dynamic behavior that only surfaces when you type and listen with a screen reader; tools can't infer that the live update should have been announced.
patterns.realWorldNote: Amy Carney's Squarespace audit: 'Search results appear on keystroke but screen readers aren't notified of appearance or result count; processing spinner lacks announcements; Quick Preview not keyboard accessible.' https://theamycarney.com/2024/04/02/observations-on-squarespace-accessibility/

patterns.platform: Wix Slideshow / Pro Gallery slider & lightbox; Wix popups
patterns.name: Carousel/slider/lightbox not keyboard operable or focus-trapping
patterns.description: Wix sliders and popups frequently can't be advanced/controlled by keyboard, and opened lightboxes/popups either don't move focus in, leave focus on the page behind, or trap it without an Esc exit. Arrow controls are mouse-only; the auto-rotating slideshow can't be paused.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Whether a control is reachable AND operable by keyboard, whether focus moves into a dialog, and whether Esc escapes are runtime/interaction facts. Static scans see divs/images; they can't exercise Tab/Enter/Esc to discover the inoperability or the trap.
patterns.realWorldNote: Wix ADA guides: 'Wix sliders are frequently keyboard inaccessible' and 'Wix popups often fail keyboard navigation.' https://www.lowcodewebsite.com/post/wix-accessibility-complete-guide-to-fix-issues-achieve-ada-compliance-2026

patterns.platform: Elementor / Divi mega-menu and dropdown nav (default Nav Menu widget, Max Mega Menu)
patterns.name: Submenu opens on hover only, not keyboard-operable, not dismissible (1.4.13)
patterns.description: The dropdown/mega-menu reveals on mouse hover via CSS :hover. Tab key skips the submenu entirely (submenus stay display:none for keyboard), and even where they appear they cannot be dismissed with Esc and aren't hoverable/persistent. Keyboard and screen-reader users cannot reach second-level items, and the hover-revealed panel fails Content on Hover or Focus.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
• Products
    • Item A
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static scanners see valid nested lists and links and report no error. Discovering that the submenu only opens on hover, that Tab never reaches it, and that Esc does not dismiss the hover panel requires actually operating the menu by keyboard and mouse.
patterns.realWorldNote: Divi 'dropdown menus can only be activated with a mouse... submenus remain hidden.' https://arrowdesign.ie/fix-divi-menu-accessibility-issues-wcag-compliance-solution/ ; WP Trac #49950 'submenu should be dismissible' (1.4.13); https://216digital.com/how-to-make-mega-menus-more-accessible/

patterns.platform: Elementor Accordion / Toggle widget, Divi Toggle/Accordion module
patterns.name: Custom accordion header not keyboard-operable / wrong tabindex / missing aria-expanded
patterns.description: Accordion headers are <div>/<a href="#"> with a jQuery click handler. The clickable element either isn't focusable, or has the wrong tabindex (Elementor puts tabindex on the wrong child so the control is invisible to keyboard), and Enter/Space don't toggle because the handler only listens for click. aria-expanded is missing or, in some builder versions, slapped onto a <summary> where it is invalid.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Section One
...
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=tab with no working keyboard handler can look structurally fine to a scanner; some tools flag missing aria-expanded but not the click-only handler. Confirming Enter/Space actually toggle the panel, and that focus lands and the expanded state is announced, requires keyboard testing.
patterns.realWorldNote: Elementor issue #23335 'Accordion and Toggle have broken accessibility'; #11246 'aria-expanded not used'; community: 'JQuery click event handler cannot be triggered via keypress.' https://github.com/elementor/elementor/issues/23335 and https://testpros.com/accessibility/making-elementor-essential-addons-accordion-accessible/

patterns.platform: Elementor Tabs widget / Beaver Builder Tabs / Divi Tabs module
patterns.name: Tab panel content not associated/announced; div tabs missing roles
patterns.description: Builder 'tabs' render as styled divs. Either the tablist/tab/tabpanel roles and aria-controls/aria-selected are absent (so it's just clickable divs), or the roles exist but the panel content isn't reliably exposed when a tab is activated. Selecting a tab by keyboard may not move focus or announce the newly revealed panel.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
• Description
  • Reviews
...
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Plain divs with click handlers raise no role/value error in a scanner (nothing claims to be a tab). Where roles do exist, confirming the active panel's content is actually announced on switch needs screen-reader testing, not static analysis.
patterns.realWorldNote: Beaver Builder review: with tabs 'the content of an expanded tab isn't reliably read out.' https://wpshout.com/beaver-builder-accessibility/

patterns.platform: Elementor / Divi 'div as button' CTA blocks, animated counters, hotspot widgets
patterns.name: Div with onClick acting as a button — wrong/absent role, no keyboard, name mismatch
patterns.description: A styled <div> (or <a href="#">) carries a JS click handler and visually reads as a button. It exposes no button role, isn't in the tab order, and Enter/Space don't activate it. Where an aria-label is added it can mismatch the visible label (e.g. visible 'Start your free trial', aria-label left as a generic 'button' from a template), so the accessible name doesn't contain the visible text.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Start your free trial
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A div with onClick and no role is invisible to the accessibility tree, so some scanners simply don't see a control to test. Detecting the visible-vs-accessible name mismatch and that it should be a keyboard-operable button requires comparing what's seen to what's announced.
patterns.realWorldNote: Elementor #25128: aria-label custom attribute doesn't reach the <a>, producing name mismatches; div-button anti-pattern is endemic to builder CTA modules. https://github.com/elementor/elementor/issues/25128

patterns.platform: Shopify / BigCommerce — quick-view modal (Add to cart from grid)
patterns.name: Quick-view modal keyboard trap / no focus return
patterns.description: Quick-view modals open over the product grid. Two common failures: (a) focus stays on the underlying page so keyboard users tab through background content behind the overlay, or (b) focus enters the modal but Escape doesn't close it and Tab can cycle but never escape, and on close focus is not returned to the triggering 'Quick view' button — keyboard users are stranded or lose their place.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: role=dialog may be present so structural checks pass. The trap, the missing Escape handler, and the failure to restore focus to the trigger are dynamic, interaction-time behaviors that require actually tabbing through the open modal and closing it — automated DOM snapshots don't exercise focus flow or key handlers.
patterns.realWorldNote: TestParty's Shopify checkout/keyboard guides explicitly call out 'quick-view modals that trap focus so keyboard users cannot escape' and modals that 'capture focus and never give it back'. https://testparty.ai/blog/shopify-checkout-keyboard-navigation-fixes ; https://testparty.ai/blog/modal-dialog-accessibility

patterns.platform: Shopify / WooCommerce — AJAX filter / faceted search sidebar
patterns.name: Facet filtering updates grid silently; no result-count announcement
patterns.description: Selecting a filter checkbox (size, color, price) re-renders the product grid via AJAX with no page reload. The new result count ('24 products') and any 'No results' state are not in a live region, so screen reader users don't know the grid changed or how many products remain. Some themes also replace native checkboxes with styled divs that lose keyboard operability.
patterns.typicalMarkup: 24 products
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: On the initial static snapshot the markup is valid (labeled checkboxes, a count div). The defect appears only when a filter fires and content swaps without an announcement — a runtime behavior. Whether the count and no-results state qualify as status messages requiring aria-live is an intent-based judgment scanners can't make.
patterns.realWorldNote: Equalize Digital's FacetWP audit and Scott O'Hara's 'dynamic results' guidance cover exactly this; accessibility-test.org documents ecommerce faceted-search live-region gaps. https://equalizedigital.com/testing-facetwp-for-accessibility/ ; https://accessibility-test.org/blog/compliance/accessibility-for-e-commerce-product-filtering-and-faceted-search/

patterns.platform: Wix Stores / headless React storefronts — icon-only controls
patterns.name: div/span 'button' with visual label mismatching its accessible name
patterns.description: Cart, wishlist, quick-add and quantity controls are built as <div> or <span> with click handlers and an icon. Either there is no accessible name at all, or an aria-label was copy-pasted/templated so it mismatches the visible glyph or tooltip (e.g. a heart icon labeled 'button', or a '+' quantity stepper whose aria-label says 'Decrease'). The visible text/icon and the programmatic name disagree.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A linter flags the second case (clickable span with no name / no role / no keyboard handler) — that part is auto-detectable. But the first case has a role, tabindex, and an aria-label, so axe passes it; detecting that the label 'Decrease' contradicts the visible '+' glyph requires reading the icon and comparing it to the name — a visual/semantic human judgment (the 'accessible name contains visible label' check needs human eyes on the icon).
patterns.realWorldNote: Wix guidance notes 'missing or inappropriately applied ARIA labels' as a critical screen-reader issue and that some elements need manual fixing; TestParty lists wishlist/quick-add 'icon-only buttons without labels'. https://accessibe.com/blog/knowledgebase/wix-website-accessibility ; https://testparty.ai/blog/beyond-alt-text-hidden-shopify-accessibility-barriers

patterns.platform: Webflow div with Interaction (IX2) used as a button/CTA
patterns.name: Clickable div CTA with no role and no accessible name
patterns.description: Designers wire a Webflow click Interaction onto a plain Div Block (often containing only an icon or a background image), so the rendered element is a clickable div with no button/link role, not in the tab order, and no accessible name. It looks and behaves like a button visually but is invisible/inoperable to keyboard and screen-reader users.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A bare <div> with a click handler attached via a data-w-id Interaction has no role, no tabindex, and frequently no text — automated scanners do not flag a generic div as a 'control' because nothing in the static DOM declares it interactive; they cannot tell it carries a JS click handler that makes it a de-facto button. Recognizing it as a missing-name control requires a human to see it renders/behaves as a CTA.
patterns.realWorldNote: Webflow's own accessibility guidance warns that click triggers should be placed on button elements rather than divs, and that role=button on a div still loses platform behaviors like spacebar activation. See Webflow accessibility checklist / 'The Webflow Way' accessibility docs: https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist and community guidance at https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management

patterns.platform: Webflow native Slider component
patterns.name: Off-screen carousel slides keep focusable controls and links
patterns.description: Webflow's Slider hides non-active slides with CSS transforms/opacity (not display:none), so links, buttons, and form fields inside the off-screen slides remain in the tab order. Keyboard users tab into invisible content, focus disappears off-screen, and the slide-dot/arrow controls are often unlabeled icon buttons.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Shop now
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The off-screen slide is still visible to the accessibility tree (no display:none / aria-hidden), so scanners see normal in-DOM links and report nothing wrong; detecting that focus visually 'leaves the screen' onto a translated-off slide requires running the keyboard sequence and watching where the focus ring goes — a dynamic, visual check tools don't perform.
patterns.realWorldNote: Accessibility guidance for sliders specifies off-screen slides must be hidden via display:none/visibility:hidden or aria-hidden + tabindex=-1, which Webflow's default Slider does not do: https://dev.to/jasonwebb/how-to-build-a-more-accessible-carousel-or-slider-35lp and https://www.flowradar.com/answer/fix-issue-slider-webflow-not-accessible-screen-readers

patterns.platform: Webflow native Lightbox component
patterns.name: Lightbox opens without focus trap, dialog role, or labeled close
patterns.description: Webflow's built-in Lightbox opens an overlay but does not trap focus (Tab leaves the modal to the page behind it), has no role=dialog / aria-modal, no accessible name on the dialog, and the close 'X' is an unlabeled icon. Esc behavior and focus return to the trigger are not handled.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: A missing focus trap is a behavioral property: nothing in the static markup is 'invalid', so axe/Lighthouse cannot detect that Tab escapes the open overlay. The unlabeled close MIGHT be flagged, but confirming the dialog lacks a name and that focus returns to the trigger requires opening it and operating it by keyboard.
patterns.realWorldNote: Documented that the Webflow lightbox lacks a focus trap (users can tab out), is missing a descriptive accessible name on the dialog, and needs custom code/ARIA to fix: https://www.gracefulwebstudio.com/blog-articles/webflow-video-lightbox-accessibility-and-focus-management and Webflow's own checklist task 'Ensure modals are keyboard navigable': https://webflow.com/accessibility/checklist/task/ensure-modals-are-keyboard-navigable

patterns.platform: Webflow / Framer hover-revealed dropdown menus and tooltips
patterns.name: Hover content (mega-menu, tooltip) not dismissible, hoverable, or persistent
patterns.description: Mega-menu panels and tooltips built as hover-only Interactions appear on mouseover and vanish the instant the pointer leaves the trigger. There's no Esc-to-dismiss, the revealed panel can't be hovered into without it closing, and it isn't reachable/persistable by keyboard focus.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Products
Item AItem B
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Dismissible/hoverable/persistent (1.4.13) are interaction-time properties. Static analysis sees a nav item with a nested panel and can't determine the panel only appears on :hover, disappears when the pointer moves toward it, and lacks an Esc handler — this requires a human to hover and try to interact with the revealed content.
patterns.realWorldNote: Classic 1.4.13 failure: content disappears when the mouse moves off the trigger and offers no Esc dismissal; design tools' hover Interactions reproduce exactly this: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/content-on-hover-or-focus.html and https://sarahmhigley.com/writing/tooltips-in-wcag-21/

patterns.platform: Bootstrap Modal (and hand-rolled React modals)
patterns.name: Background page not inert / aria-hidden focus conflict behind modal
patterns.description: When a Bootstrap/custom modal opens, the underlying page is not made inert and is not hidden from AT (or, conversely, aria-hidden="true" is placed on an ancestor that still contains the focused trigger). Screen-reader users can read and tab into the page behind the dialog, and focus can land on aria-hidden content, producing the "focusable element inside aria-hidden" conflict.
patterns.typicalMarkup: ...
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe flags aria-hidden containing a focusable element only when the snapshot is in that exact state; whether the background is truly inert / focus is trapped is a runtime, interaction-driven property. Confirming a SR can reach behind-modal content or that Tab escapes requires actually operating the dialog with the keyboard/AT.
patterns.realWorldNote: Bootstrap issue #29769 and MDN's aria-modal docs cover the inert/aria-hidden tradeoff; the focusable-inside-aria-hidden conflict is a frequent audit finding. https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/29769

patterns.platform: jQuery UI / Bootstrap Tabs & Accordion
patterns.name: div/anchor "tab" widgets lacking tab roles and arrow-key support
patterns.description: Older jQuery UI and many Bootstrap-derived tab/accordion implementations render tabs as <a>/<li> or plain divs that toggle panels via click, without role="tablist"/"tab"/"tabpanel", without aria-selected/aria-controls, and without the expected arrow-key roving-tabindex behavior. Screen readers do not recognize the tab pattern and keyboard users cannot move between tabs with arrow keys.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
• Details
  • Reviews
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Plain anchors with hrefs are individually valid and focusable, so structural linters see nothing wrong. Recognizing that this SHOULD be the ARIA tabs pattern (and that arrow-key navigation and aria-selected are absent) requires understanding the intended widget semantics and testing keyboard interaction.
patterns.realWorldNote: WAI-ARIA APG tabs pattern requires roles + arrow-key support; legacy jQuery UI / Bootstrap tab markup commonly ships without them, a recurring audit finding for interactive widgets.

patterns.platform: Tabs widget (Bootstrap nav-tabs, hand-rolled tab UIs)
patterns.name: Tabs with no roving tabindex / no arrow-key support
patterns.description: Tab strips use role="tablist"/role="tab" markup (or just styled links) but every tab is a separate Tab stop and arrow keys do nothing. Users must Tab through all tabs, and roving tabindex (one tabindex=0, rest -1) is absent, breaking the APG keyboard contract. Often aria-selected is also static or missing.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
• Overview
  • Specs
  • Reviews
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: axe has a 'tablist must contain tabs' structural check but does not verify the roving-tabindex pattern or arrow-key handling — those are runtime keyboard behaviors. A page where every tab is independently Tab-focusable is technically operable, so it does not fail any static rule; the broken expectation (arrow keys move between tabs) is only observable by operating it.
patterns.realWorldNote: MDN tab/tablist role docs and Deque's A11y Support Series both specify roving tabindex (active tab tabindex=0, others -1) and arrow-key navigation as the contract that custom tabs routinely omit. https://www.deque.com/blog/a11y-support-series-part-1-aria-tab-panel-accessibility/

patterns.platform: Menu button + role=menu (app 'kebab' menus, navigation 'mega menus')
patterns.name: role=menu misused for site nav; no arrow keys, no haspopup, links not menuitems
patterns.description: Developers slap role="menu"/role="menuitem" onto a navigation dropdown of links, or onto an actions menu, but never implement the APG menu keyboard model: no aria-haspopup on the trigger, no focus moved to the first item on open, arrow keys do nothing, Escape does not close. Because role=menu changes how screen readers expose children (links stop being announced as links), the result is worse than plain markup.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
• Profile
  • Log out
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The ARIA is syntactically valid (menu contains menuitems), so structural rules pass. The failures are behavioral (missing arrow-key navigation, focus not entering the menu, Escape not closing) plus a semantic judgment that role=menu was the wrong pattern for navigation links — neither is visible in a static DOM scan.
patterns.realWorldNote: The Zenyth 'Navigating the Maze of ARIA Menu Roles' guide and APG menubar pattern stress that role=menu is for application menus, demands full arrow-key focus management, and is routinely misapplied to site navigation. https://www.zenythgroup.com/post/navigating-the-maze-of-aria-menu-roles-a-comprehensive-guide

patterns.platform: Custom slider (price range filters, noUiSlider clones, hand-rolled drag handles)
patterns.name: Slider with no role/value and no keyboard operation
patterns.description: A draggable thumb on a track is built from divs with a mousedown handler. There is no role="slider", no aria-valuenow/min/max, no aria-valuetext, and arrow keys do nothing. Screen reader users hear no value and cannot change it; keyboard-only users cannot operate it at all. Dual-thumb range sliders compound this by giving neither thumb a name.
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: If the thumb has no role and no tabindex, axe sees only inert divs and cannot know they are meant to be a slider, so it raises nothing. Even when role=slider is present, whether arrow keys actually change aria-valuenow is a runtime behavior. The intent ('this draggable thing is a value control') requires visually recognizing the slider, which a linter cannot do.
patterns.realWorldNote: TPGi's 'ARIA Slider' series and DigitalA11y's slider-role reference state authors MUST set aria-valuemin/max/now and must update value + aria-valuetext on every arrow/Home/End keypress — the steps custom sliders most often skip. https://www.tpgi.com/aria-slider-part-1/

patterns.platform: Carousel / slider (Slick, Swiper defaults, hero banners on CMS themes)
patterns.name: Auto-rotating carousel with no pause control and no slide announcement
patterns.description: A hero carousel auto-advances every few seconds with no visible/operable pause-stop-hide control. Slides change under keyboard focus, focus is lost when the focused slide rotates away, off-screen slides remain in the tab order and accessibility tree, and slide changes are not exposed via group/aria-roledescription/live region. Vestibular and cognitive users get unstoppable motion; keyboard users get focus thrown to the top of the page.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Big Sale
New In
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Auto-rotation, the absence of a pause control, focus loss when slides swap, and links inside hidden slides remaining tabbable are all timing/runtime behaviors. A static scan cannot tell the content is moving or that a pause mechanism is required; deciding whether off-screen slides are correctly hidden needs observing the rotation. WebAIM notes carousels are 'one of the most problematic' widgets precisely for these reasons.
patterns.realWorldNote: WebAIM 'Animation and Carousels' and the APG carousel pattern require a pause/stop control, pausing on focus, and hiding non-visible slides; Smashing Magazine's accessible-carousel guide documents the focus-loss-on-rotate bug. https://webaim.org/techniques/carousels/

patterns.platform: ARIA tree / file-explorer tree (CMS page-tree pickers, doc nav trees)
patterns.name: Tree with Tab-per-node instead of arrow navigation; missing expanded/level
patterns.description: A nested expand/collapse tree uses role="tree"/role="treeitem" but is navigated with Tab to every node (instead of a single tab stop + arrow keys), parent nodes lack aria-expanded, end nodes wrongly carry aria-expanded, and aria-level/setsize/posinset are absent on dynamically loaded branches. Screen reader users get no hierarchy or open/closed state; the keyboard model contradicts the APG tree contract.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
• Docs
    • Intro
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The role nesting (tree > treeitem > group) is structurally valid so static checks pass. Whether arrow keys navigate, whether the tree is a single tab stop, and whether aria-expanded toggles on expand/collapse are runtime behaviors. Knowing aria-expanded is missing on a parent requires knowing which nodes have children at runtime — invisible to a snapshot scan.
patterns.realWorldNote: MDN tree/treeitem role docs and Accessible Culture's '(Not so) Simple ARIA Tree Views' document that trees use arrow-key navigation (not Tab), require aria-expanded only on parents, and need aria-level/setsize/posinset on dynamic nodes — all routinely botched. https://accessibleculture.org/articles/2013/02/not-so-simple-aria-tree-views-and-screen-readers/

patterns.platform: Radio group (custom styled radios, form-builder widgets, Shoelace-style components)
patterns.name: Custom radios: no grouping, every radio a tab stop, no arrow selection
patterns.description: Styled radio buttons are built from divs (or are native radios stripped of fieldset/legend and group semantics). There is no role="radiogroup" or fieldset/legend, so the question text is never associated; each radio is a separate Tab stop instead of one stop with arrow-key selection; and the group label is unannounced. Screen reader users hear isolated options with no context or count.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Choose a plan

Basic
Pro
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss:
Individual role=radio elements with text content pass name/role checks. The missing radiogroup association (the 'Choose a plan' label is a sibling

, not a programmatic group name) and the broken single-tab-stop + arrow-key model are a structural-relationship judgment and a runtime behavior respectively — TestParty reports 95% of sites have at least one improperly grouped radio set that scanners do not catch as a hard failure.
patterns.realWorldNote: TestParty's radio-group remediation writeup and shoelace-style/shoelace issue #218 document ungrouped radios and Tab-per-radio (instead of arrow navigation) as pervasive custom-component failures. https://testparty.ai/blog/accessible-radio-groups-html-fast-remediation-large-sites and https://github.com/shoelace-style/shoelace/issues/218

patterns.platform: Listbox (custom <select> replacements, country/option pickers)
patterns.name: Custom listbox: options not announced, selection state visual-only
patterns.description: A fake select shows a styled options panel of <li> items. The trigger lacks combobox/button semantics with aria-expanded, the panel is not role="listbox" with role="option" children, selection is shown only by a checkmark/highlight (no aria-selected), and focus/active option is not tracked. Screen reader users cannot tell which option is selected or how many exist; keyboard arrow navigation through options is often missing.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
United States
  • United States
  • Canada
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: The trigger div has an accessible name and the list is a valid <ul>, so static checks pass. That selection is conveyed only by a CSS class/checkmark (no aria-selected — a use-of-color/visual-only-state issue) and that arrow-key navigation is absent are visual and runtime judgments. The freeCodeCamp and Chris Henrick writeups stress native <select> is far safer precisely because these get botched.
patterns.realWorldNote: freeCodeCamp's accessible custom-dropdown guide and Chris Henrick's 'Custom and Accessible Select Menus Aren't Easy' document missing role=listbox/option, missing aria-selected, and absent keyboard support as the standard custom-listbox failures. https://www.freecodecamp.org/news/how-to-build-an-accessible-custom-dropdown-select-element/

patterns.platform: WordPress slider plugins (Slider Revolution, Smart Slider), Elementor/Divi carousels, Wix Pro Gallery
patterns.name: Auto-rotating carousel, keyboard-inaccessible, no pause
patterns.description: A hero carousel auto-advances on a timer with no pause/stop control, prev/next arrows are non-focusable divs, and slide changes are not announced. Keyboard users cannot reach controls; the moving content steals reading position; offscreen slides may still be in the tab order as hidden focusable links.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Shop the sale
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Auto-rotation timing and the absence of a pause control are temporal/behavioral and not in the static DOM signature. Tools may catch a div with onclick lacking a role, but cannot verify keyboard reachability of the rotation, that focus is trapped/lost between slides, or that offscreen slides leak into the tab order — all need manual keyboard testing.
patterns.realWorldNote: WCAG-ART and the A11Y Collective document carousel pause/keyboard/announce failures as classic manual-test items: https://www.a11y-collective.com/blog/accessible-carousel/ ; WP slider accessibility caveats: https://www.abrightclearweb.com/accessible-slider-wordpress/

patterns.platform: Bootstrap/template tabs, accordions, and custom dropdowns in CMS themes
patterns.name: Custom widget role present but state/keyboard support missing
patterns.description: A theme implements tabs/accordions/menus with role=tab/button and ARIA, satisfying role checks, but the dynamic VALUE/STATE is wrong or static: aria-expanded never toggles, aria-selected is hard-coded, the panel relationship (aria-controls) is broken, and arrow-key navigation is absent. ARIA presence makes the page LOOK accessible while behaving inaccessibly.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
<button aria-expanded="false" class="accordion">Shipping</button>
<!-- clicking opens the panel visually but aria-expanded stays "false"; no arrow-key support -->
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Static scans confirm the ATTRIBUTES exist and are valid; they cannot verify the attribute VALUE tracks the live UI state (aria-expanded staying false after opening) or that keyboard interaction patterns work — these are dynamic, requiring activation and re-inspection. This is precisely why WebAIM finds MORE detected errors on ARIA-heavy pages.
patterns.realWorldNote: WebAIM Million: pages WITH ARIA average ~34-69% MORE detected errors than pages without — broken/incomplete ARIA is a leading cause: https://webaim.org/projects/million/2024 ; 2026 confirms the pattern: https://webaim.org/projects/million/

patterns.platform: Marketing-site / CMS clickable cards and tiles built as div/span with onclick (Webflow interactions, custom hero tiles, jQuery .click handlers)
patterns.name: div/span with click handler as a fake button (no role, no keyboard)
patterns.description: An interactive control is a bare div or span with a JS click handler, no role, no tabindex, and only an onclick (no keydown). Keyboard users cannot reach or activate it, and screen readers announce nothing meaningful. This is the canonical W3C F59 failure.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Pricing

See plans
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Partially auto-detectable (axe 'interactive controls must be operable' / clickable element flags exist), but tools frequently miss it when the handler is attached via addEventListener at runtime rather than an inline onclick attribute, or delegated from a parent. Confirming it is genuinely interactive (vs. a decorative animated div) often needs a human to click/Tab and observe.
patterns.realWorldNote: W3C failure F59 (script makes div/span a UI control without a role); Deque 'Building Accessible Buttons with ARIA'. https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20-TECHS/F59.html

patterns.platform: Modal dialogs, off-canvas drawers, and carousels (Bootstrap modal backdrops, slick/swiper slides, third-party overlay libs) that set aria-hidden on containers holding focusable elements
patterns.name: aria-hidden="true" on (or wrapping) focusable elements
patterns.description: A container is hidden from AT with aria-hidden="true" but still contains tabbable controls (links, buttons, inputs) that were not made inert / tabindex=-1. Keyboard users can Tab into a control the screen reader refuses to announce — 'focus goes nowhere' — producing a phantom/ghost focus and broken navigation. Common on inactive carousel slides and behind-modal page content.
patterns.typicalMarkup: Buy now
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: Mostly auto-detectable (axe rule 'aria-hidden elements do not contain focusable elements'). Included for completeness. Tools can miss it when focusability comes from runtime-added tabindex, or when the aria-hidden is toggled on only in a state (modal open) the scanner never enters; reaching that state is a human/dynamic step.
patterns.realWorldNote: GetWCAG 4.1.2 fix guide 'avoid focusable elements inside aria-hidden containers'; ACT rules issue 643; UW accessibility 'aria-hidden elements'. https://getwcag.com/en/accessibility-guide/aria-hidden-focus

patterns.platform: Page-builder custom widgets (Elementor/WPBakery div "buttons", custom controls with aria-label)
patterns.name: div role=button whose accessible name contradicts its visible label
patterns.description: A builder renders an interactive control as a <div>/<span> with role="button" (or no role at all) and an aria-label that was authored separately from the visible text — so the on-screen label says "Submit" while the accessible name is "Send form", or the visible text is "Get Quote" but aria-label is "button". Voice-control users saying the visible word can't activate it, and screen-reader users hear something different from what's shown; when role is missing entirely, it isn't even reachable by keyboard.
patterns.typicalMarkup:
Submit
Get Quote
patterns.whyAutoToolsMiss: When an aria-label is present the control HAS an accessible name, so 4.1.2 "has a name" passes; comparing that name against the visible rendered text to detect a mismatch requires OCR/text extraction of the visible label and a semantic equality judgment that automation doesn't make reliably. (The pure missing-role/not-focusable variant is more linter-catchable.)
patterns.realWorldNote: div role=button with aria-label diverging from visible text is the canonical accessible-name-mismatch failure (also a 2.5.3 issue). https://www.makethingsaccessible.com/guides/say-what-you-see-wcag-2-5-3-label-in-name-level-a/ and https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/failures/F96.html
